key_insight: RoboTTT shows that robot policies can use extremely long visuomotor context—up to 8K timesteps—without increasing inference latency. This enables new capabilities like one-shot imitation from human video and on-the-fly policy improvement.
problem_solved: Most robot foundation models only use single-step or short-history context, which limits their ability to learn from long demonstrations, adapt during deployment, and handle complex temporal dependencies.
method: Introduces Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a model and training recipe designed for very long context windows.
Scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps, far beyond prior robot policies, while keeping inference latency essentially unchanged.
Uses the extended context at test time to support in-context imitation, rapid adaptation, and improved robustness to perturbations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work suggests that longer context can unlock qualitatively new robot behaviors without sacrificing real-time performance. It provides a practical path toward more adaptable, data-efficient robot policies that can learn from demonstrations and respond to changing conditions.
visual_elements: A side-by-side timeline showing short-context policies vs. RoboTTT's 8K-step context window
A pipeline diagram of the RoboTTT training and test-time adaptation process
An icon-based comparison of capabilities: imitation, adaptation, and robustness
A latency chart illustrating that longer context does not increase inference time
paper_title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge
